title: Position and Movement: Grids, Coordinates and Maps
seo_title: Grade 6 Position and Movement Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Locate positions on a grid with alphabetical and numerical grid references; locate and give directions to specified positions on a map or grid; describe movement between positions using compass directions.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 position and movement worksheets: grid references, coordinates, compass directions and following directions. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Grid reference: letter, then number. Coordinate: across, then up.
key_sub: Give a direction and a number of squares.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A grid reference names a square: letter (column) first, then number (row): D3.
  • A coordinate names a point: (x, y). Go across first, then up: (4, 2).
  • Compass directions: N, E, S, W and NE, NW, SE, SW in between.
  • Give directions with a direction and a number of squares.

Examples

Example

From (2, 3), move 4 right and 1 up

x: 2 + 4

y: 3 + 1

Answer: (6, 4)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
y firstAcross first, then up.
East and westEast is on the right with north at the top.
Counting the startCount the moves only.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about position and movement?
faq.a: Locate positions on a grid with alphabetical and numerical grid references, and describe and follow directions to move between positions on a map or grid.
On maps, in games and on graphs.

items.q: What is in square C1?
items.e: Go across to column C first, then down to row 1. Square C1 is the library. Reading the number as the column (column A, row 3) gives the fire station.

items.q: What is in square E2?
items.e: Go across to column E first, then down to row 2. Square E2 is the chemist. Reading the number as the column (column B, row 5) gives the train station.

items.q: What is in square A3?
items.e: Go across to column A first, then down to row 3. Square A3 is the fire station. Reading the number as the column (column C, row 1) gives the library.

items.q: What is in square F3?
items.e: Go across to column F first, then down to row 3. Square F3 is the bus stop.

items.q: What is in square B4?
items.e: Go across to column B first, then down to row 4. Square B4 is the police station.

items.q: What is in square E5?
items.e: Go across to column E first, then down to row 5. Square E5 is the vet.

items.q: What is in square D4?
items.e: Go across to column D first, then down to row 4. Square D4 is the supermarket.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the bakery?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The bakery is in column F, row 1: F1. Always write the letter first, so not 1F.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the pool?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The pool is in column A, row 2: A2. Always write the letter first, so not 2A.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the café?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The café is in column E, row 3: E3. Always write the letter first, so not 3E.

items.q: Which picture shows the table with 4 chairs from above (a bird’s-eye view)?
items.e: A bird’s-eye view shows something from above, like a bird flying over it. Picture C shows the table with 4 chairs from above. Picture A shows it from the side.

items.q: Which picture shows the car from above (a bird’s-eye view)?
items.e: A bird’s-eye view shows something from above, like a bird flying over it. Picture A shows the car from above. Picture B shows it from the side.

items.q: Which picture shows the cup of hot chocolate from above (a bird’s-eye view)?
items.e: A bird’s-eye view shows something from above, like a bird flying over it. Picture B shows the cup of hot chocolate from above. Picture A shows it from the side.

items.q: Which picture shows the tree from above (a bird’s-eye view)?
items.e: A bird’s-eye view shows something from above, like a bird flying over it. Picture D shows the tree from above. Picture A shows it from the side.

items.q: Which picture shows the house from above (a bird’s-eye view)?
items.e: A bird’s-eye view shows something from above, like a bird flying over it. Picture D shows the house from above. Picture A shows it from the side.

items.q: This is a bird’s-eye view. What is it?
items.e: You can see a pillow at one end and a blanket. It is a bed seen from above.

items.q: This is a bird’s-eye view. What is it?
items.e: A round top with 4 small circles around it: a round table with 4 stools, seen from above.

items.q: This is a bird’s-eye view. What is it?
items.e: You can see the windscreen, the roof and the 4 wheels poking out. It is a car seen from above.

items.q: A drink can stands on a table. What shape does its top look like in a bird’s-eye view?
items.e: From above you see only the round top of the can: a circle. From the side the can looks like a rectangle.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the sink?
items.e: Go across first to find the letter, then down to find the number. The sink is in column E, row 2: E2. Always write the letter first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 3 on the x-axis, then up to 5. Point A is at (3, 5). Across first, then up: the x-coordinate is written first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 6 on the x-axis, then up to 2. Point A is at (6, 2). Across first, then up: the x-coordinate is written first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 1 on the x-axis, then up to 4. Point B is at (1, 4). Across first, then up: the x-coordinate is written first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 7 on the x-axis, then up to 6. Point B is at (7, 6). Across first, then up: the x-coordinate is written first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point C?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 4 and do not go up at all: the point is on the x-axis. Point C is at (4, 0). The x-coordinate is written first.

items.q: Which point is at (2, 5)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 2 on the x-axis, then up to 5. The point is at (2, 5). Across first, then up: the x-coordinate is written first. That is point B.

items.q: Which point is at (6, 3)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 6 on the x-axis, then up to 3. The point is at (6, 3). Across first, then up: the x-coordinate is written first. That is point D.

items.q: Which point is at (5, 7)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 5 on the x-axis, then up to 7. The point is at (5, 7). Across first, then up: the x-coordinate is written first. That is point A.

items.q: Which point is at (0, 6)?
items.e: x = 0 means you do not go across at all. Go straight up the y-axis to 6. That is point C. (6, 0) is on the x-axis instead.

items.q: In the coordinates (3, 7), which number tells you how far to go across?
items.e: The first number is the x-coordinate: how far across. The second number is the y-coordinate: how far up. (3, 7) is 3 across and 7 up.

items.q: What is the point (0, 0) called?
items.e: (0, 0) is where the x-axis and the y-axis meet. It is called the origin. You start counting from there.

items.q: Which point is on the y-axis?
items.e: Every point on the y-axis has x-coordinate 0, because you do not go across. (6, 0) is on the x-axis.

items.q: On a map grid of a school excursion to the zoo, north is up the page. Pieter starts at (1, 2) and walks 3 squares east and 2 squares north to the lion enclosure. What are the coordinates of the lion enclosure?
items.e: East and west change x; north and south change y. East 3 squares changes x: 1 + 3 = 4. North 2 squares changes y: 2 + 2 = 4. The new point is (4, 4).

items.q: On a map grid of a school camp, north is up the page. Amahle starts at (7, 6) and walks 4 squares west and 3 squares south to the dining hall. What are the coordinates of the dining hall?
items.e: East and west change x; north and south change y. West 4 squares changes x: 7 − 4 = 3. South 3 squares changes y: 6 − 3 = 3. The new point is (3, 3).

items.q: On a map grid of the botanic gardens, north is up the page. Refilwe starts at (2, 8) and walks 5 squares east and 6 squares south to the lily pond. What are the coordinates of the lily pond?
items.e: East and west change x; north and south change y. East 5 squares changes x: 2 + 5 = 7. South 6 squares changes y: 8 − 6 = 2. The new point is (7, 2).

items.q: Karabo is at (4, 6) on a map grid where north is up. Her friend is at (4, 2). In which direction should she walk to reach her friend?
items.e: x stays 4, so there is no move east or west. y goes from 6 down to 2, which is down the page: south.

items.q: On a map grid of a school, north is up the page. The tuck shop is at (2, 3) and the library is at (7, 3). How do you walk from the tuck shop to the library?
items.e: y stays 3, so there is no move north or south. x goes from 2 up to 7: 7 − 2 = 5 squares to the right, which is east. Count squares, not lines (that gives 6).

items.q: A rectangle has three corners at (1, 1), (6, 1) and (6, 4). What are the coordinates of the fourth corner?
items.e: The fourth corner is above (1, 1) and across from (6, 4). So it has x-coordinate 1 and y-coordinate 4: (1, 4).

items.q: How many squares apart are the points (2, 6) and (9, 6)?
items.e: The y-coordinates are the same, so the points are on the same row. Take the x-coordinates: 9 − 2 = 7 squares. Counting the lines, including the first one, gives 8.

items.q: Elna wants to plot the point (2, 5). She goes 5 across and then 2 up. What mistake did she make?
c: She should go down, not up
items.e: Across first, then up. (2, 5) means 2 across and 5 up. Elna plotted (5, 2) instead.

items.q: The zebras are ___ of the wild dogs.
items.e: The wild dogs are in C3 and the zebras are in D2. From the wild dogs, go 1 square right (east) and 1 square up (north). The same number each way is a diagonal, so the zebras are north-east of the wild dogs. Check east (right) and west (left) carefully: north-west would be the other way.

items.q: The reptiles are ___ of the ostriches.
items.e: The ostriches are in C1 and the reptiles are in A3. From the ostriches, go 2 squares left (west) and 2 squares down (south). The same number each way is a diagonal, so the reptiles are south-west of the ostriches. Check east (right) and west (left) carefully: south-east would be the other way.

items.q: The toilets are ___ of the entrance.
items.e: The entrance is in C5 and the toilets are in B4. From the entrance, go 1 square left (west) and 1 square up (north). The same number each way is a diagonal, so the toilets are north-west of the entrance. Check east (right) and west (left) carefully: north-east would be the other way.

items.q: The play area is ___ of the seals.
items.e: The seals are in E3 and the play area is in F4. From the seals, go 1 square right (east) and 1 square down (south). The same number each way is a diagonal, so the play area is south-east of the seals. Check east (right) and west (left) carefully: south-west would be the other way.

items.q: The tortoise is ___ of the zebras.
items.e: The zebras are in D2 and the tortoise is in D4. From the zebras, go 2 squares down (south). So the tortoise is south of the zebras.

items.q: The café is ___ of the aviary.
items.e: The aviary is in E1 and the café is in F1. From the aviary, go 1 square right (east). So the café is east of the aviary.

items.q: The lions are ___ of the reptiles.
items.e: The reptiles are in A3 and the lions are in A1. From the reptiles, go 2 squares up (north). So the lions are north of the reptiles.

items.q: The reptiles are ___ of the wild dogs.
items.e: The wild dogs are in C3 and the reptiles are in A3. From the wild dogs, go 2 squares left (west). So the reptiles are west of the wild dogs.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight north-west from the wild dogs?
items.e: North-west is up and to the left on the map. From the wild dogs (C3), move one square at a time diagonally: the first place is the meerkats in B2. Going north-east by mistake gives the zebras.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight north-east from the entrance?
items.e: North-east is up and to the right on the map. From the entrance (C5), move one square at a time diagonally: the first place is the tortoise in D4. Going north-west by mistake gives the toilets.

items.q: The oval is ___ of the garden.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The oval is east of the garden. Do not mix up east and west: “Never Eat Soggy Weet-Bix” goes round clockwise: north, east, south, west.

items.q: The tuck shop is ___ of the toilets.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The tuck shop is north of the toilets.

items.q: The art room is ___ of the tuck shop.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The art room is south of the tuck shop.

items.q: The library is ___ of the hall.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The library is east of the hall. Do not mix up east and west: “Never Eat Soggy Weet-Bix” goes round clockwise: north, east, south, west.

items.q: The hall is ___ of the office.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The hall is west of the office. Do not mix up east and west: “Never Eat Soggy Weet-Bix” goes round clockwise: north, east, south, west.

items.q: The bike racks are ___ of the classrooms.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The bike racks are south of the classrooms.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight north from the garden?
items.e: North is up on the map. Go north from the garden, square by square. The first place you reach is the library. Going south would give the sandpit.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight west from the garden?
items.e: West is to the left on the map. Go west from the garden, square by square. The first place you reach is the toilets. Going east would give the oval.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight north from the sandpit?
items.e: North is up on the map. Go north from the sandpit, square by square. The first place you reach is the garden.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight south from the library?
items.e: South is down on the map. Go south from the library, square by square. The first place you reach is the garden.

items.q: Lungile starts at the red dot in B4. He goes 3 squares east. Which square does he finish in?
items.e: Start at B4. Go 3 squares east to E4. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at D4.

items.q: Themba starts at the red dot in E5. He goes 3 squares north. Which square does he finish in?
items.e: Start at E5. Go 3 squares north to E2. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at E3.

items.q: Johan starts at the red dot in F2. He goes 4 squares west. Which square does he finish in?
items.e: Start at F2. Go 4 squares west to B2. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at C2.

items.q: Thandi starts at the red dot in A1. She goes 3 squares south-east. Which square does she finish in?
items.e: Start at A1. Go 3 squares south-east to D4. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at C3.

items.q: Jabu starts at the red dot in E5. He goes 2 squares north-west, then 1 square north. Which square does he finish in?
items.e: Start at E5. Go 2 squares north-west to C3, then 1 square north to C2. Swapping the two numbers of squares gives D2.

items.q: Anika starts at the red dot in B5. She goes 2 squares north-east, then 2 squares east. Which square does she finish in?
items.e: Start at B5. Go 2 squares north-east to D3, then 2 squares east to F3. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at D4.

items.q: Naledi starts at the red dot in F1. She goes 2 squares south-west, then 2 squares south. Which square does she finish in?
items.e: Start at F1. Go 2 squares south-west to D3, then 2 squares south to D5. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at E3.

items.q: Andile starts at the red dot in A3. He goes 3 squares east, then 2 squares north. Which square does he finish in?
items.e: Start at A3. Go 3 squares east to D3, then 2 squares north to D1. Mixing up north and south gives D5.

items.q: Start at the gate. Go 1 square south-east, then 3 squares east. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at A1. Go 1 square south-east to B2, then 3 squares east to E2. The gum tree is in E2. Swapping the two numbers of squares gives the sandpit.

items.q: Start at the car park. Go 4 squares north, then 2 squares west. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at F5. Go 4 squares north to F1, then 2 squares west to D1. The swings are in D1. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at the gum tree.

items.q: Amahle starts at the red dot. She goes 2 squares east. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at C4. Go 2 squares east to E4. That is square B. If you mix up east and west you land on A.

items.q: Yusuf starts at the red dot. He goes 3 squares north. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at E5. Go 3 squares north to E2. That is square A. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on B.

items.q: Kgomotso starts at the red dot. She goes 3 squares west. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at E2. Go 3 squares west to B2. That is square D. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Ravi starts at the red dot. He goes 3 squares south. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at C1. Go 3 squares south to C4. That is square C. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Thandi starts at the red dot. She goes 3 squares east, then 2 squares north. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at A5. Go 3 squares east to D5, then 2 squares north to D3. That is square A. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on B.

items.q: Daniel starts at the red dot. He goes 1 square north, then 3 squares west. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at F5. Go 1 square north to F4, then 3 squares west to C4. That is square D. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Tebogo starts at the red dot. He goes 2 squares south, then 3 squares east. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at B1. Go 2 squares south to B3, then 3 squares east to E3. That is square B. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Anika starts at the red dot. She goes 2 squares west, then 3 squares north. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at E4. Go 2 squares west to C4, then 3 squares north to C1. That is square C. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Start at the gate. Go 2 squares north, then 2 squares east. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at A5. Go 2 squares north to A3, then 2 squares east to C3. The gum tree is in C3.

items.q: Start at the BBQ. Go 3 squares east, then 1 square north. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at A3. Go 3 squares east to D3, then 1 square north to D2. The bench is in D2.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (2, 3) and B is at (5, 1). Across: 2 to 5 is 3 squares right. Up and down: 3 to 1 is 2 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (6, 2) and B is at (3, 6). Across: 6 to 3 is 3 squares left. Up and down: 2 to 6 is 4 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (3, 6) and B is at (3, 1). The x-coordinate stays 3, so there is no move left or right. Up and down: 6 to 1 is 5 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (1, 5) moves to (6, 1) in B. That is 5 squares right and 4 squares down. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (1, 1) moves to (6, 5) in B. That is 5 squares right and 4 squares up. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (6, 5) moves to (1, 1) in B. That is 5 squares left and 4 squares down. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: A corner of a shape moves from (2, 7) to (8, 3). Describe the translation.
items.e: The start is at (2, 7) and the end is at (8, 3). Across: 2 to 8 is 6 squares right. Up and down: 7 to 3 is 4 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: A corner of a shape moves from (9, 1) to (5, 6). Describe the translation.
items.e: The start is at (9, 1) and the end is at (5, 6). Across: 9 to 5 is 4 squares left. Up and down: 1 to 6 is 5 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is at (3, 4). It is translated 2 squares right and 3 squares up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Right 2 squares changes x: 3 + 2 = 5. Up 3 squares changes y: 4 + 3 = 7. The new point is (5, 7).

items.q: Point A is at (2, 7). It is translated 5 squares right and 4 squares down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Right 5 squares changes x: 2 + 5 = 7. Down 4 squares changes y: 7 − 4 = 3. The new point is (7, 3).

items.q: Which directions take you from the gate to the sandpit?
items.e: The gate is in A1 and the sandpit is in E4. A to E is 4 squares east. Row 1 to row 4 is 3 squares south. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which directions take you from the slide to the toilets?
items.e: The slide is in C1 and the toilets are in A4. C to A is 2 squares west. Row 1 to row 4 is 3 squares south. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which directions take you from the car park to the BBQ?
items.e: The car park is in F5 and the BBQ is in B2. F to B is 4 squares west. Row 5 to row 2 is 3 squares north. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which directions take you from the rotunda to the kiosk?
items.e: The rotunda is in C5 and the kiosk is in F1. C to F is 3 squares east. Row 5 to row 1 is 4 squares north. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which directions take you from the tap to the skate park?
items.e: The tap is in F2 and the skate park is in A5. F to A is 5 squares west. Row 2 to row 5 is 3 squares south. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which one straight line takes you from the tap to the rotunda?
items.e: The tap is in F2 and the rotunda is in C5. That is 3 squares west and 3 squares south: the same number each way, so it is a diagonal. Go 3 squares south-west.

items.q: Which one straight line takes you from the toilets to the swings?
items.e: The toilets are in A4 and the swings are in D1. That is 3 squares east and 3 squares north: the same number each way, so it is a diagonal. Go 3 squares north-east.

items.q: Which one straight line takes you from the car park to the sandpit?
items.e: The car park is in F5 and the sandpit is in E4. That is 1 square west and 1 square north: the same number each way, so it is a diagonal. Go 1 square north-west.

items.q: Which directions describe the dashed path from the BBQ to the swings?
items.e: Start at B2. Go 2 squares east to D2, then 1 square north to D1. That is the swings.

items.q: Which directions describe the dashed path from the gate to the rotunda?
items.e: Start at A1. Go 2 squares south to A3, then 1 square east to B3, then 2 squares south to B5, then 1 square east to C5. That is the rotunda.
